record.paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
record.original_question: Find algebraic graph-theoretic characterizations of colored graphs that represent closed piecewise-linear 4-manifolds whose fundamental groups lie in specified classes such as finite groups, free products, surface groups, poly-(finite or cyclic) groups, or amenable groups. A colored graph represents a closed PL n-manifold when its associated colored-graph polyhedron is PL homeomorphic to that manifold.

artifact.category_tag: colored graphs and crystallizations of PL manifolds
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on crystallizations/gems for PL 4-manifolds (e.g., work on simple crystallizations, gem-complexity, and trisections from colored triangulations) provides partial results characterizing certain restricted families (simply-connected manifolds, manifolds with small gem-complexity, etc.) but no general graph-theoretic characterization of 5-colored graphs representing closed PL 4-manifolds whose fundamental group lies in the listed classes (finite, free products, surface groups, poly-(finite or cyclic), amenable) appears available. The problem remains open in its general form.

status_evidence.title: PL 4-manifolds admitting simple crystallizations
status_evidence.snippet: Simple crystallizations characterize certain simply-connected PL 4-manifolds by graph invariants such as gem-complexity equal to 3β₂(M).
status_evidence.claim: Only partial characterizations exist, mostly in the simply-connected setting.

status_evidence.title: Cataloguing PL 4-manifolds by gem-complexity
status_evidence.snippet: Catalogues PL 4-manifolds by gem-complexity; characterizations cover only small-complexity cases.
status_evidence.claim: General characterization by fundamental-group class is not provided.

status_evidence.title: A graph-theoretical representation of PL-manifolds — A survey on crystallizations
status_evidence.snippet: Survey notes that algebraic/graph-theoretic recognition of 4-manifold crystallizations by fundamental-group type remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem is listed as open in the crystallization survey literature.
